subject: science
passage: Most biologists do not classify viruses as living organisms, chiefly because a virus cannot reproduce or carry out metabolism on its own: outside a host cell, it is an inert package of genetic material wrapped in protein. The discovery in 2003 of mimivirus, a virus larger than some bacteria, prompted renewed debate, but it has not overturned this view. ______ mimivirus and the other giant viruses identified since then carry genes for some of the molecular machinery that cells use to build proteins, machinery that ordinary viruses lack. Yet none of these viruses possesses ribosomes, the structures in which proteins are actually assembled, so even the largest of them remain wholly dependent on the cells they infect.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The author's position is that giant viruses have not overturned the view that viruses are not alive. The sentence with the blank states a fact that seems to favor the other side (the genes for protein-building machinery), and the next sentence begins "Yet," returning to the author's position. The blank must introduce a concession.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Indeed" would strengthen the preceding claim that the view has not been overturned, but the genes for protein-building machinery point the other way. This is the most tempting choice because it would fit if the passage stopped after "prompted renewed debate."
explanation.B: Incorrect. The genes are not a result of the view surviving; they are what made the debate arise.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The genes are not an example of the view remaining intact; they are evidence that seems to challenge it.
explanation.D: Correct. "Granted" concedes a point in favor of the opposing view before "Yet" explains why that point is not decisive.
